<Group>
A small bakery opens at six. The ovens are warm by five, the first loaves come out at half past, and the counter is
stocked before the door unlocks. None of that is visible to the people waiting outside.

What they see is the shelf. If it is full, the morning went to plan. If it is half empty, something upstream slipped
and the rest of the day is spent catching up.

</Group>

<Group>
<QuietTitle>A typical morning looks like this:</QuietTitle>

1. Mix the dough the evening before and let it rest overnight in the cold room.
2. Shape the loaves at four, while the ovens heat up.
3. Bake in two rounds, so the second batch is still warm at nine.

</Group>

The routine is simple because every step has a fixed time. Nobody has to decide anything at five in the morning.

<Section id="ovens" label="The ovens">
<Eyebrow>01 — The ovens</Eyebrow>

## Two ovens, one schedule

Each oven holds twelve trays. The first round fills both, the second round fills one, and the spare oven keeps pastry
warm until the lunch crowd arrives.

- Bread goes in the top oven.
- Pastry goes in the bottom oven, which runs cooler.

<TextTable
  items={[
    {"title": "Top oven.", "text": "Bread, at the highest heat, in two rounds."},
    {"title": "Bottom oven.", "text": "Pastry and anything that browns too quickly up top."}
  ]}
/>

When one oven fails, the schedule still holds: bread moves down, pastry waits.

</Section>

The shelf is full again by nine, and the
day starts over tomorrow.
